transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-22 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ben Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Redwood), John Park (ACME CTO), Lisa Chen (ACME ML), Tom Alvarez (ACME Infra)
Shared artifacts: redwood-optimize-deck.pdf (link), benchmark-template.xlsx (link), security-brief.pdf (link)

[00:00] Ben: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ben from Redwood, AE for your account, this is Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] John: Good, thanks. We want to understand how batching and the KV cache can help our real-time credit scoring pipelines, mainly around cost and tail latency.
[00:18] Priya: Great, we'll walk through recommended configs, show cost model examples, and then talk pilot steps. Quick baseline question, what's your current qps and average prompt length?
[00:27] Lisa: Right now it's around 30 QPS steady, spikes to 120 during peak, median prompt tokens about 120, response tokens ~80. There's some prefix that repeats across requests - customer metadata and a small conversation history.
[00:41] Priya: OK that maps well to a mixed workload where prefix caching helps. Quick note on terms: when I say 'prefix cache' I mean automatic prefix KV-cache-- sometimes transcribers write KV cash or kayvee cash, but it's KV cache (key-value).
[00:55] Tom: We're on GCP, using private VPCs, VPC-SC, and we need to ensure we can use a customer-managed KMS. Also SOC2 is required.
[01:07] Ben: Absolutely, we can do VPC peering or private endpoints for Dedicated, and Private deployment supports customer KMS/HSM. We'll send the security brief.
[01:15] Priya: Demo slide 1: batching. The core idea is to increase throughput by grouping similar requests so we amortize attention computations. For ACME you'd get higher token throughput at the cost of slight added queuing delay.
[01:29] Lisa: How does that affect your p95 latency? Our SLO is 200ms for scoring.
[01:34] Priya: With aggressive batching you'll see increased p50 and p95; for instance on a 8-GPU node pool we measured p95 of 180ms at 30QPS with batch size 8, but at 120QPS you need autoscaling or reserved capacity to keep p95 under 200ms.
[01:49] Ben: Important tradeoff: hosted (pay-as-you-go) vs dedicated reserved capacity. Dedicated gives predictable latency and lower unit cost at scale.
[01:58] John: Can you show the cost model for prefix vs KV cache?
[02:03] Priya: Sure. Slide: cost model assumptions: token cost per GPU-second, cache hit rate, average tokens saved per hit. Example: if you have a 40% KV cache hit rate and save 30 tokens per request, that's a 12 token per request reduction on average, multiply by request volume and you get big savings.
[02:20] Marta: And prefix cache applies only to repeated initial segments; KV cache stores intermediate KV states for autoregressive generation which is great for conversational or multi-turn scoring.
[02:33] Lisa: Our scoring uses the same context prefix (account info) across many requests, so prefix cache seems ideal. We're less conversational except we maintain a tiny turn history.
[02:43] Priya: So recommendation: enable prefix caching for your prefix-heavy fields and enable KV caching for the small multi-turn contexts. In practice you can combine both: prefix cache reduces early token recompute, KV cache speeds up generation for the remainder.
[02:56] Tom: Are there memory or GPU changes for KV cache? We worry about memory pressure on nodes.
[03:02] Priya: Good question. KV cache increases memory per request because we store key/value tensors. We typically size an instance pool with headroom - e.g., gtx-32 configs or A100 configs and use autoscaler to handle spikes. There are quantized cache formats to reduce memory too.
[03:18] Ben: We have an 'Optimize' recommendation engine that suggests batch sizes and cache TTLs based on your latency SLO and token distribution.
[03:27] John: Can the Optimize suggestions be run against a sample of our traffic or is it generic?
[03:31] Priya: We run it on your sample or our benchmark harness. For the pilot we'll ingest 10k requests, run permutations for batch sizes (1,4,8,16) and KV cache hit rates (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%) to produce a cost/latency matrix.
[03:47] Lisa: How do you model the added queuing delay for batching?
[03:50] Priya: We use request arrival distribution to estimate queuing and tail latencies; our simulator adds queue delay proportional to batch formation time and then model kernel throughput. It's an approximation but aligns with measured runs ~85% of the time.
[04:03] Tom: From security: how is cache data encrypted at rest and who controls keys?
[04:09] Ben: For Private deployments you control keys via KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we offer customer-managed keys and audit logs; cache shards at rest are encrypted. We'll include this in the security brief.
[04:20] John: Any concerns about PII in cache? We have strict retention rules.
[04:24] Priya: TTL + eviction policies are configurable. You can set zero retention for sensitive fields and use tokenization/PII filtering before caching. Also RBAC and audit logs trace cache access.
[04:37] Marta: I'll note that our console shows per-route token savings and cost delta if you enable KV or prefix cache - we can demo that in the console later.
[04:47] Ben: Quick live demo: Priya will toggle batching in the console and show the cost model spreadsheet.
[04:52] Priya: (screen share) Here's Optimize -> Workloads -> ACME-sample. You can see suggested batch size 8, predicted p95 190ms, and estimated cost reduction 27% at 30QPS with 40% cache hit. If we go to batch size 16 cost drops more but p95 rises over 250ms.
[05:12] Lisa: That matches why we can't push batch too high.
[05:15] Priya: Right, and you can constrain by per-route latency SLO - Optimize will respect that threshold and only suggest configs that stay within it.
[05:25] Tom: Can we test with our sample in a sandbox?
[05:28] Ben: Yes. Proposed pilot: 2-week sandbox with dedicated small pool, run 10k request benchmark, analyze cost/latency matrix, then propose reserved plan.
[05:38] John: What's pricing for sandbox?
[05:40] Ben: We'll provide a pilot quote; usually credit-backed demo or short-term reserved and then invoice. I'll send details.
[05:46] Lisa: One more thing - multi-region routing. We need to keep data in EU for GDPR.
[05:51] Priya: We support region pinning and Private deployments in customer region. For Hosted we have region options and data residency controls.
[05:59] John: Any notes about fallback when capacity is constrained? We can't have failures.
[06:03] Priya: Optimize and the runtime support fallbacks to smaller/quantized variants of the model and cross-region fallback; also automatic burst capacity for Dedicated. We'll show logs of graceful degradation later.
[06:15] Marta: Ok quick recap of recommended settings for ACME initial pilot: batch size 8, enable prefix cache for static account prefix, enable KV cache for 2-turn contexts with 20s TTL, reserved capacity equivalent to handling 120QPS peak with autoscale headroom.
[06:34] Lisa: Sounds good. Can you put numbers on expected monthly savings?
[06:38] Priya: Based on sample: with 30QPS and 40% hit rate you save ~25-30% token compute cost. At scale 120QPS savings compound so saved dollars are larger. We'll send the model spreadsheet.
[06:50] John: Any competitive differentiators for Optimize vs other vendors?
[06:54] Ben: We focus on production economics and provide per-route cost visibility, model/quantization recommendations, and automatic prefix/KV caching tied to SLOs. Competitors often require manual tuning or don't expose unit economics cleanly.
[07:10] Tom: Ok procurement will need SOC2 docs and encrypted logs - we'll get procurement on the thread.
[07:16] Ben: I'll attach SOC2 summary and security brief.
[07:20] Priya: Next steps: we'll run the benchmark, share pilot pricing, and set a follow-up in two weeks to review results.
[07:27] John: Great. Anything else?
[07:30] Lisa: Quick clarification: if we enable prefix cache, is that opaque to our code or do we need instrumentation?
[07:35] Priya: No code change usually - it's a switch in the routing or SDK; we recommend instrumenting with our tracing hooks to monitor cache hit rates.
[07:45] Ben: Alright, we'll recap via email with links. Thanks everyone.
[07:49] John: Thanks all.

[End of transcript]
notes: Transcript has minor transcription artifacts (KV cache sometimes transcribed as KV cash). Customer concerned about PII retention and multi-region data residency. Pilot agreed: 2-week sandbox + 10k request benchmark. AE to send pricing and SOC2 docs. SE to run bench and provide cost/latency matrix.
